fbi:
## Origins in the 1910s control architecture

Badlands Media commentary dates the Bureau's creation to 07/26/1908, describing it as the national police force required before a broader campaign of national control could get underway.[n] Known first as the Bureau of Investigation (BOI), the agency changed its name to the Federal Bureau of Investigation in 1935; it began with 34 employees and has grown to roughly 35,000 with a publicly acknowledged annual budget of $10 billion.[n] In its infancy the BOI's first task was to surveil houses of prostitution in preparation for enforcement of the [[mann-act|Mann Act]], the "white slave traffic act" — a focus the article contrasts sarcastically with a modern Bureau said to assign 80 agents to look for mean tweets.[n] The article notes that a Hollywood producer arrested for running a prostitution ring for elites was being pursued by the FBI on Mann Act charges, remarking that there is nothing new under the sun.[n]
mann-act:
## Early enforcement and the Bureau of Investigation

Badlands Media commentary describes the Mann Act, otherwise known as the "white slave traffic act," as the statute whose anticipated enforcement gave the newly formed [[fbi|Bureau of Investigation]] its first assignment: surveilling houses of prostitution.[n] The article contrasts a Bureau of 34 employees singularly focused on ending sex slavery with a modern FBI of 35,000 that, in the author's view, is not.[n] It also notes the act's continued use, citing the arrest of a Hollywood producer accused of running a prostitution ring for elites — with accusers claiming they were drugged, held prisoner and forced into prostitution — whom the FBI pursued on Mann Act charges.[n]
hollywood:
## Founding as a propaganda system (1910s)

Badlands Media commentary presents Hollywood as the propaganda arm installed once a national police force was in place.[n] The first movies were made in Europe in the 1890s, and their potential to influence the general public was quickly recognized; in October 1911 the first Hollywood movie studio opened on Sunset Boulevard, and within a year fifteen more studios had followed.[n] The stated reason for the influx into Southern California was the weather, which permitted year-round filming and allowed the region to mimic locations around the world.[n] By 1924 movies had become the seventh largest industry in America and, in the article's framing, the country's number one propaganda tool.[n]

## Babylon and predictive programming

The article discusses the Brad Pitt film *Babylon*, released in late December 2022, which depicts the depravity of the 1920s Hollywood scene — drugs, excessive drinking, elite deaths swept under the rug, and a scene in which stars must flatter the [[rothschild-family|Rothschilds]] as financiers of Hollywood movies.[n] The author reads the film as predictive programming that desensitizes and normalizes such depravity, while interpreting the film's silent-to-talkies transition as a metaphor for society moving past Hollywood's spell — its transition toward insignificance.[n] With film established in the 1910s, broadcast radio followed in the 1920s and television in the 1940s, giving what the article calls the elite cabal a propaganda tool that reached everyone and left America a slave to Hollywood propaganda.[n]
john-d-rockefeller:
## Pivot from oil to medicine

At the beginning of the twentieth century John D. Rockefeller had become the richest man in America through his monopolization of the oil industry, and Badlands Media commentary argues that when the Model T Ford — first produced in Detroit in 1908 — made automobiles and thus gasoline demand accessible to the masses, he transitioned into the medical industry.[n]

Rockefeller is credited with moving medicine from mostly homeopathic and natural treatment to an allopathic, petrochemical model, so that remedies drawn for centuries from natural sources would instead come from chemicals.[n] He bought shares in the German pharmaceutical company [[ig-farben|I.G. Farben]], later one of Nazi Germany's largest firms, and mounted a smear campaign portraying natural healing modalities as quackery.[n] With [[andrew-carnegie|Andrew Carnegie]] he founded medical schools teaching only allopathic medicine, and the [[american-medical-association|American Medical Association]] was formed to recognize only chemical-based practitioners.[n] The [[rockefeller-institute-hospital|Rockefeller Institute Hospital]] opened in 1910 as the first center for clinical research and, in the article's phrase, the birthplace of virology and of [[big-pharma|Big Pharma]].[n] After the Spanish Flu subsided, Rockefeller-run pharmaceutical companies rolled out vaccines and claimed credit for ending the outbreak.[n]
american-medical-association:
## Role in the allopathic transition

Badlands Media commentary describes the American Medical Association as forming alongside the allopathic medical schools founded by [[john-d-rockefeller|John D. Rockefeller]] and [[andrew-carnegie|Andrew Carnegie]], and states that the AMA would recognize only people who practiced allopathic, chemical-based medicine.[n] Paired with Rockefeller's smear campaign against natural healing modalities and the 1910 opening of the [[rockefeller-institute-hospital|Rockefeller Institute Hospital]], this arrangement meant that anyone who did not follow the guidelines of the new medical industry — a pill for every illness — could not practice medicine in America.[n]
ig-farben:
## Rockefeller investment

Badlands Media commentary states that [[john-d-rockefeller|John D. Rockefeller]] bought shares of I.G. Farben, a pharmaceutical company based in Germany that would become one of Nazi Germany's biggest companies, as part of his shift from oil into the medical industry and the broader transition of American medicine from natural to petrochemical treatment.[n]
jekyll-island-club:
## The November 1910 meeting

In November 1910 six men — [[nelson-aldrich|Nelson Aldrich]], A. Piatt Andrew, Henry Davison, Arthur Shelton, Frank Vanderlip and [[paul-warburg|Paul Warburg]] — met at the Jekyll Island Club off the coast of Georgia.[n] Badlands Media commentary states that these men represented wealthy banking interests including [[jp-morgan|J.P. Morgan]], the Rockefellers and the [[rothschild-family|Rothschilds]], and that they gathered in secret to write a plan to reform the nation's banking system.[n] The plan drafted on Jekyll Island laid the foundation for what would become the [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve System]].[n]
federal-reserve:
## Jekyll Island origins and the 1913 vote

Badlands Media commentary traces the Federal Reserve to a secret November 1910 meeting at the [[jekyll-island-club|Jekyll Island Club]] off the Georgia coast, where six men — [[nelson-aldrich|Nelson Aldrich]], A. Piatt Andrew, Henry Davison, Arthur Shelton, Frank Vanderlip and [[paul-warburg|Paul Warburg]] — representing [[jp-morgan|J.P. Morgan]], the Rockefellers and the [[rothschild-family|Rothschilds]] drafted a plan to reform the nation's banking system.[n] The article recounts the theory that the [[rms-titanic|Titanic]] was sunk in 1912 to eliminate three wealthy opponents of the plan aboard — [[benjamin-guggenheim|Benjamin Guggenheim]], [[isidor-straus|Isa Strauss]] and [[john-jacob-astor|John Jacob Astor]] — and to warn others against speaking out.[n]

Because the American public was vehemently opposed and most congressmen regarded a yes vote as political suicide, the article says a surprise vote was taken on 12/23/1913, when most of Congress had left for the holidays and only those paid to pass it remained.[n] The result was a private system of Wall Street bankers controlling the money supply and interest rates, issuing money backed by nothing — described as the fox guarding the henhouse.[n]

## Inflation and the interest burden

The article argues that money printed from nothing and injected into the supply creates inflation, so that a 1913 dollar now has the purchasing power of about two cents, whereas an 1800 dollar retained roughly the same purchasing power a century later.[n] Because the bankers charged the United States interest on money they created, a federal income tax was needed to pay that interest — linking the Fed to the [[sixteenth-amendment|16th Amendment]] and the revived [[internal-revenue-service|IRS]] of the same year and completing what the author calls [[debt-slavery|debt slavery]].[n] The same Wall Street and Federal Reserve bankers, it adds, financed both sides of every major war for over a century.[n]
internal-revenue-service:
## Civil War origins and 1913 revival

Badlands Media commentary notes that the IRS had existed since 1862, formed to collect money for the [[american-civil-war|Civil War]], and largely faded afterward once there was no longer a real need for it.[n] The agency was reformed on 2/25/1913 — a few weeks after ratification of the [[sixteenth-amendment|16th Amendment]] on 2/3/1913 and ten months before the [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]] was created.[n] The article argues the new income tax existed to pay interest to the bankers running the Federal Reserve, and that because Americans balked at the idea the tax began at one percent and rose gradually, boiling-frog fashion, to modern rates; had it begun at 15 or 20 percent, it contends, there would have been another revolution.[n] It calls 1913 a worse year than 2020, as it produced the IRS, the income tax and the Federal Reserve together.[n]
sixteenth-amendment:
## 1913 ratification in the Badlands account

Badlands Media commentary states that the 16th Amendment created an income tax on Americans in 1909 but was not ratified until 2/3/1913 — a few weeks before the [[internal-revenue-service|IRS]] was brought back on 2/25/1913 and ten months before the [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]] was established.[n] The article asks why an income tax was needed when existing taxes seemed to get the job done, and answers that it was required to pay interest to the bankers who printed money out of nothing for the Federal Reserve.[n] It notes the tax started at one percent to overcome public resistance and was raised slowly thereafter, so that today no one knows a time without income taxes.[n]
edward-bernays:
## Freudian roots of public relations

Badlands Media commentary identifies Edward Bernays as the American nephew of [[sigmund-freud|Sigmund Freud]], who graduated from Cornell University in 1912 and chose journalism as a career.[n] He began applying his uncle's techniques and understanding of the unconscious mind, becoming the father of public relations and arguably of modern advertising.[n] In his 1928 book *Propaganda*, Bernays wrote that propaganda is not merely beneficial but necessary in governing a nation.[n] The article places him at the center of its claim that the 1910s were the decade Americans began to be altered, affected and controlled on an unconscious level — brainwashed — alongside the arrival of [[psychoanalysis]] in America through [[james-jackson-putnam|James Jackson Putnam]] and the [[american-psychoanalytic-association|American Psychoanalytic Association]].[n]
planned-parenthood:
## 1916 founding in the Badlands account

Badlands Media commentary states that 1916 gave America Planned Parenthood, started by a group of racists seeking to control the population and eliminate the gene pool of groups they viewed as inferior.[n] It asserts that clinics were set up mostly in Black neighborhoods in an attempt to reduce or eliminate Black people from American society, and the author offers the opinion that legal abortion became the greatest Satanic child sacrifice system the world has ever known.[n] The founding is counted among the institutional developments of the 1910s that the article calls the decade Americans became slaves.[n]
spanish-flu:
## Pandemic fear as a control mechanism

Badlands Media commentary dates the Spanish Flu to 1917 and describes it as having created an opportunity to control populations through fear of pandemics — a pattern the author says was seen firsthand with COVID.[n] After the Spanish Flu died off, the article states, [[john-d-rockefeller|Rockefeller]]-run [[big-pharma|Big Pharma]] companies rolled out their vaccines and claimed they were the reason the outbreak ended.[n] The episode is listed among the 1910s developments the author groups under the heading of mass enslavement.[n]
world-war-i:
## 1914 and the banker-warlord system

Badlands Media commentary states that 1914 gave the world its first global war and a war-like system that still dominates today, in which wars are used to take control of civilizations while enriching the financial backers of those wars.[n] It alleges that the same Wall Street and [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]] bankers have financed both sides of every major war for more than a century — including the Nazis and the Allies, the operators of WWII concentration camps, those who intentionally starved millions of Soviet Ukrainians in the 1930s, and those in charge of the killing fields in Cambodia.[n] WWI, in this framing, was the start of the perfect marriage between bankers who control the money and warlords who create wars to take over civilizations and economies.[n]
erik-carlson:
## "The Decade We All Became Slaves"

On March 22, 2023, Erik Carlson published "The Decade We All Became Slaves" for Badlands Media, a historical essay arguing that the 1910s installed the systems of control — the [[fbi|FBI]], [[hollywood]], [[big-pharma|Big Pharma]] and [[debt-slavery|debt slavery]] — that still bind Americans today.[n] The piece opens by contesting the standard account of the [[american-civil-war|Civil War]] as a war to free the slaves, arguing it was fought over money, and traces how [[sharecropping]] made post-emancipation life harder for many former slaves.[n] It closes with an exhortation to raise expectations, hold institutions accountable and free one's own mind, noting that a group of Patriots working behind the scenes cannot do the public's homework for it.[n] Carlson invites readers to find more of his work at his own Substack.[n]

american-civil-war:
## A war over money, not slavery

Badlands Media commentary argues that although Americans are taught the war of the 1860s was fought to free the slaves, it was fought over money like every other war.[n] The article accepts as true the observation that the North was overwhelmingly Republican and the South overwhelmingly Democrat, but rejects the moral framing built on it.[n] It describes the South as an agricultural juggernaut without real competition and the North as an industrial region facing stiff European competition: the South could afford to leave the United States and start its own country, but the North could not afford to lose the South.[n] The North had more people and the South more money, allowing the North to vote in laws that eventually required the South to pay 90 percent of the country's taxes.[n]

## Aftermath

The article disputes the idea that abolition immediately enriched former slaves, arguing that for most in the South life became harder and more cruel, as chattel ownership gave way to [[sharecropping]], which stripped landowners of any responsibility for the workers they employed.[n] It notes that at the start of the war 12 percent of Americans were slaves owned by other individuals, while today, in the author's framing, 99 percent are slaves owned by the American system.[n]
debt-slavery:
## The 1913 architecture

Badlands Media commentary presents debt slavery as the largest of the control systems installed in the 1910s, following the [[fbi|FBI]], [[hollywood]] and [[big-pharma|Big Pharma]].[n] Its machinery was assembled in a single year: ratification of the [[sixteenth-amendment|16th Amendment]] on 2/3/1913, the reforming of the [[internal-revenue-service|IRS]] on 2/25/1913, and the surprise holiday-season congressional vote of 12/23/1913 that created the [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]].[n] Money printed from nothing and lent at interest created enduring inflation — a 1913 dollar now buys about two cents' worth — and the income tax exists, in this account, to service the interest owed to the bankers.[n]

## Modern shackles

The article concludes that where antebellum slaves could not leave the plantation, modern Americans are shackled by debt, mortgages, taxes and the necessity of participating in the system to survive, convinced they are free while having nowhere to run.[n] It urges readers to reset their expectations, hold institutions accountable, and direct their time and money away from companies they regard as abusive, arguing that the Cabal's ultimate goal is for people to have nothing and be satisfied with it.[n]

Rockefeller]]'s move from oil into medicine at the start of the twentieth century, which converted American practice from largely homeopathic and natural treatment to an allopathic, petrochemical model.[n] Rockefeller bought shares in the German firm [[ig-farben|I.G. Farben]], smeared natural healing as quackery, and with [[andrew-carnegie|Andrew Carnegie]] founded medical schools teaching only allopathic medicine, while the [[american-medical-association|American Medical Association]] recognized only chemical-based practitioners.[n] The 1910 opening of the [[rockefeller-institute-hospital|Rockefeller Institute Hospital]] — the first center for clinical research and, the article says, the birthplace of virology — marks the birth of Big Pharma, after which physicians who rejected a pill for every illness could not practice in America.[n] Following the [[spanish-flu|Spanish Flu]], Rockefeller-run pharmaceutical companies rolled out vaccines and claimed credit for ending the outbreak.[n]

john-jacob-astor:

Badlands Media commentary names John Jacob Astor as one of three wealthy businessmen aboard the [[rms-titanic|Titanic]] in 1912 — with [[benjamin-guggenheim|Benjamin Guggenheim]] and [[isidor-straus|Isa Strauss]] — who are said to have opposed the formation of a [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]].[n] The article recounts the theory that the ship was sunk to eliminate their opposition and to send a message to others who spoke against the plan drawn up at the [[jekyll-island-club|Jekyll Island Club]], while presenting it explicitly as a theory.[n]

rms-titanic:

Badlands Media commentary recounts the theory that the Titanic was sunk in 1912 because three wealthy businessmen aboard — [[benjamin-guggenheim|Benjamin Guggenheim]], [[isidor-straus|Isa Strauss]] and [[john-jacob-astor|John Jacob Astor]] — opposed forming a [[federal-reserve|Federal Reserve]].[n] In that account the sinking was meant both to eliminate their opposition and to send a message to others who might speak against the banking plan drafted at the [[jekyll-island-club|Jekyll Island Club]] in November 1910.[n] The article presents the claim as a theory rather than established history.[n]

harvard-university:
## Psychoanalysis in America

Badlands Media commentary notes that [[james-jackson-putnam|James Jackson Putnam]], Professor of Diseases of the Nervous System at Harvard, encountered the work of [[sigmund-freud|Sigmund Freud]], and that his public endorsement represented a significant breakthrough for the psychoanalytic cause in the United States, leading in 1911 to the founding of the [[american-psychoanalytic-association|American Psychoanalytic Association]] with [[ernest-jones|Ernest Jones]].[n]
